verdictDetail: The 60-period integrated model, the 12/36/60 views, the cash/VAT/inventory/working-capital identities, the 24 stress cases and the conditional break-even thresholds recompute exactly from the curated inputs (0 mismatches) and the COST-16 tooling invariant holds. The frozen candidate is nevertheless NOT approved: the mandatory delivery record D21 MC-13-DELIVERY.md is absent so the gate is 71/73 (D-02 fails) and the unit-suite positive control fails; the adversarial suite is additionally state-dependent and cannot reach 29/29 at the final record; the Spanish executive report asserts an independent-review PASS that was never awarded and contradicts the manifest and the MC-14 handoff; the refund/returns allowance is never settled as cash, which overstates cash and reverses the direction of stress ST-07; and distributor receivables/invoiced cash are computed at full list price x 1.21 without the declared 35% distributor margin. findings.title: Refund/returns allowance reduces revenue and VAT but is never paid in cash, overstating cash and the direction of an adverse stress case
findings.evidence: Engine scripts/marea-financial-engine.mjs computes refundsAllowance from gross invoices and deducts it from net revenue and output VAT, but cashReceiptsGross stays gross of refunds and no refund cash outflow column exists. Correcting the cash flow by paying the allowance in the sale month: BASE cumulative cash M60 -415,478.92 -> -477,860.35 (-62,381.43, total refunds) and financing requirement 987,326.73 -> 1,008,167.43 (+20,840.70); DOWNSIDE -3,075,765.77 -> -3,083,784.12 and 3,075,765.77 -> 3,083,784.12; UPSIDE 5,440,764.18 -> 5,277,822.48 and 632,135.66 -> 635,750.07. Stress ST-07 (warranty/returns 6%) currently reports cumulativeCashDeltaVsBaseEur = +10,608.01 and financingRequirementDeltaVsBaseEur = -3,398.50, i.e. an adverse case improves cash and reduces the funding requirement; corrected, it is -51,773.42 versus the corrected base. MC13-WORKING-CAPITAL-AND-CASHFLOW.md §3.3 labels the allowance a 'non-cash deduction' while §9 claims 'higher returns reduce net revenue and cash' - the second statement is contradicted by the model.
findings.description: The refund treatment is economically inconsistent: it removes revenue and remitted VAT as if the sale had not happened, yet assumes the customer still pays the gross price and never refunds it. Cash and financing requirement are therefore overstated in favour of the candidate, and the ST-07 stress case is presented as adverse although it improves the computed cash position. The auditor cash-refund control shows the existing identities cannot absorb a refund-cash column, so the gate cannot see this defect.
findings.requiredCorrection: Decide and implement one consistent treatment: (a) preferred - add a refunds cash outflow (month of sale or a declared lag), reduce cash receipts and output VAT accordingly, extend the working-capital/cash identities and validator checks, regenerate all derived files and refresh every document figure and the ST-07 row; or (b) if refunds are to remain a non-cash allowance, stop reducing output VAT on refunded sales and restate the cash bridge, but then explain why collected cash is retained. Correct the contradictory D10 §9 statement and the ST-07 direction in every human-readable report.
findings.correctionOwner: financial-model owner (engine + validator + data) with the documentation owner
findings.auditorReverification: Recompute cumulative cash and financing requirement with the corrected treatment, confirm ST-07 is adverse versus the corrected base and that the documents quote the corrected figures.

findings.title: Distributor receivables and distributor invoiced gross use full list price x 1.21, ignoring the declared 35% distributor margin and double-counting VAT on a VAT-inclusive price
findings.evidence: Engine buildHardwareBlock: skuReceivable[m] = round2(units[m] * grossPrice * distributorShare * (1 + vat/100)) with grossPrice = priceHypothesis.grossAmountEur (vatBasis VAT_INCLUDED) and channel mix DISTRIBUTOR_RETAIL 25% share / 35% revenue deduction. For HUB-STANDARD the modelled distributor invoice is 0.25 x 349 x 1.21 = 105.57 EUR/unit while the channel-consistent figure is 0.25 x 349 x 0.65 = 56.71 EUR/unit. Channel-consistent correction: BASE distributor invoiced total 695,041.92 -> 373,369.78, trade receivables M60 28,050.84 -> 15,068.64, financing requirement 987,326.73 -> 974,344.53 and cumulative cash M60 -415,478.92 -> -402,496.72 (12,982.20 timing difference from the uncollected last two months); DOWNSIDE receivables 4,282.78 -> 2,300.66 and UPSIDE 71,725.78 -> 38,530.38. Total cash over an extended horizon is conserved because direct receipts are correspondingly understated, so this is an allocation/timing error rather than a double count of total cash.
findings.description: The distributor invoice basis is wrong twice (margin not applied, VAT added to an already VAT-inclusive price). It materially overstates two published columns (trade receivables by 46%, distributor invoiced gross by 86% in BASE), understates direct receipts and distorts the collection timing used for the financing-requirement trough. The internal receivables identity still balances because both sides use the same wrong invoice basis, so the gate passes it.
findings.requiredCorrection: Compute distributor invoiced/collected cash from the channel-adjusted gross (apply the declared distributor margin once, no second VAT gross-up), regenerate the monthly model, scenario results, stress tests, generated figures and the receivables tables/bridges in the documents, and add a validator check tying distributorInvoicedGross to the declared channel share/margin and VAT basis.
findings.correctionOwner: financial-model owner (engine + validator + data) with the documentation owner
findings.auditorReverification: Recompute HUB-STANDARD distributor invoice per unit, the BASE/DOWNSIDE/UPSIDE receivables series and the financing requirement; verify the new validator check catches a re-applied VAT gross-up.

findings.title: Financial data contract §6 is stale and internally inconsistent with the implemented gate
findings.evidence: MC13-FINANCIAL-DATA-CONTRACT.md §6 states 'The implemented contract contains 71 checks'; the validator reports 73. Contract A-15 says operatingCashFlow = ebitdaLike - workingCapitalMovement - paymentFees, while §4.9 says payment fees are already inside the conditional contribution and must not be subtracted again; the implementation follows §4.9. The contract's A-13..A-25 identifiers are renumbered in the implementation (contract A-14 opening cash = implementation A-13; contract A-15 operating cash = implementation A-14; contract A-22 stress = implementation A-21; contract A-23 views = implementation A-22; contract A-25 negative economics = implementation A-23), and the implementation adds A-26, so check-id traceability between contract and gate is broken.
findings.description: The governing contract no longer describes the implemented validator. Reviewers and future milestones cannot rely on the check identifiers, and the contract's own operating-cash formula contradicts its economics section.
findings.requiredCorrection: Update §6 to the 73 implemented checks with the actual identifiers and behaviours, correct the A-15 formula to match §4.9, and state that adding checks is non-breaking while removing/renaming requires a contractVersion bump and decision-log entry.
findings.auditorReverification: Diff contract §6 against `node scripts/check-marea-financial-model.mjs --json` check ids/descriptions; confirm no formula contradiction remains.

findings.title: Scenario definitions declare empty scenarioAssumptionIds and portfolio break-even thresholds carry empty inputAssumptionIds, weakening lineage for 125 scenario assumptions
findings.evidence: data/scenario-definitions.json: scenarioAssumptionIds = [] for RESTRICTED_CURRENT, DOWNSIDE, BASE_HYPOTHETICAL and UPSIDE_HYPOTHETICAL while assumptions.json has 125 SCENARIO_ASSUMPTION records. data/break-even-thresholds.json: the operating/cash-flow/cumulative/financing portfolio thresholds have inputAssumptionIds = [] (engine buildBreakEven reads scenario.scenarioAssumptionIds). Contract §4.10 requires scenarioAssumptionIds[] and §4.13 requires inputAssumptionIds[]; the fields exist but are empty, so the documented lineage is nominal only.
findings.description: The 125 illustrative scenario assumptions are not linked from the scenario definitions, and the threshold register cannot show which assumptions produced each conditional threshold. This is a traceability weakness rather than a wrong number.
findings.requiredCorrection: Populate scenarioAssumptionIds with the scenario's demand, churn, renewal, activation, channel, clearance and opex assumptions, and have the break-even thresholds derive inputAssumptionIds from them; add a validator check that the arrays are non-empty for hypothetical scenarios.
findings.auditorReverification: Confirm every scenario has non-empty assumption ids and every conditional threshold resolves at least one assumption id.

findings.title: cohortAssumptions lacks the deferredRevenueRefundPct field required by the contract

findings.title: Subscription headroom figures omit the declared subscription channel factor and contradict the same document's own table
findings.evidence: MC13-RECURRING-REVENUE-AND-SAAS-ECONOMICS.md line 72 states pre-licence headroom 'EUR 71.39 / 110.72 for NAV and EUR 35.05 / 66.51 for WEATHER per account-year'. Those values are (gross price / 1.21) - known direct cost and omit the declared subscription channel factor 0.94: NAV-ESSENTIAL = 99 x 0.94 / 1.21 - 10.43 = 66.48, NAV-PRO = 103.33, WEATHER-STANDARD = 32.62, WEATHER-PRO = 62.10. findings.title: unitContributionStillPositive measures monthly aggregate contribution, not per-unit contribution, and the reports call it 'contribucion unitaria'
findings.evidence: Engine runStressCase: unitContributionStillPositive = knownVariableContribution[HORIZON-1] > 0, i.e. the month-60 aggregate variable contribution. stress-tests.json summary reports 23/24 true and MC13-EXECUTIVE-REPORT.md lines 175-177 and MC13-SENSITIVITY-AND-STRESS-TESTS.md present this as 'contribucion unitaria' together with a cumulative contribution figure (ST-24: 508,512.77). Several SKUs have negative per-unit contribution (HUB-STANDARD -20.10, AIS-RECEIVER -95.11, SENSE-ENTRY-SYMBOLIC -14.22), so the portfolio aggregate can be positive while the per-unit claim is unsupported.
findings.description: The field name and the Spanish wording promise a per-unit metric but the computation is a monthly aggregate. The demonstrated ST-24 behaviour (positive aggregate contribution with no cash recovery) is still true, but the label is misleading and could be read as claiming positive unit economics for every product.
findings.requiredCorrection: Rename the field/flag to reflect the actual aggregate metric (e.g. monthlyContributionPositive or aggregateContributionPositive) or compute a genuine per-unit contribution metric; update D13/D20 wording and the generated register.
findings.correctionOwner: financial-model owner with the documentation owner
findings.auditorReverification: Check the renamed field definition and all document wording against the stress-tests.json value.

findings.title: RESTRICTED_CURRENT monetary cash/tax columns are stored as zero rather than null as required by contract §4.9
findings.evidence: MC13-FINANCIAL-DATA-CONTRACT.md §4.9 requires RESTRICTED_CURRENT monetary cost/cash columns to be null with suppression reasons. data/monthly-financial-model.json RESTRICTED_CURRENT stores cashReceiptsGross, tradeReceivablesEnd, vatCollected, vatOutput and refundsAllowance as 60 zeros, while cogsHardware, fixedOpexEnvelope, EBITDA-like, operating/net/cumulative cash and financing are null. The zero revenue masks and grossInvoicedRevenue = 0 are explicitly required by the same paragraph, so the text is partly self-contradictory.
findings.description: A literal contract reader sees non-null monetary columns in the restricted case. The zeros are economically correct (no authorized revenue means no collections or receivables), but the contract text and the data disagree.
findings.requiredCorrection: Clarify §4.9: revenue, refunds, VAT output and collections derived from the zero authorized revenue are zero; cost, expense, cash balance and financing columns are null/unknown. Optionally store the former as zero with an explicit note, or null them and derive zero from the mask.
findings.auditorReverification: Compare the amended §4.9 text with the restricted columns.

findings.title: Manifest evidenceCounts cover 152 of 153 assumption records because the OFFICIAL_LICENSING_DOCUMENT category is not counted
findings.evidence: data/assumptions.json contains 153 records: 125 SCENARIO_ASSUMPTION, 11 ENGINEERING_ASSUMPTION, 7 PUBLISHED_TARIFF, 1 INHERITED_ASSUMPTION, 1 VERIFIED_OBSERVED, 7 UNKNOWN and 1 OFFICIAL_LICENSING_DOCUMENT (ASM-MC13-002). data/manifest.json evidenceCounts lists every category except the official licensing document, so its declared categories total 152. The contract's §4.1 evidenceCounts schema also has no official-document field.
findings.description: A small completeness gap in the evidence inventory; no financial output depends on it.
findings.requiredCorrection: Add an officialLicensingDocuments count (value 1) to the manifest and contract schema, or document why that class is excluded from the inventory.
findings.auditorReverification: Recount evidence classes and compare with the manifest.

findings.title: CI workflows do not execute the MC-13 financial gate, so the passing PR check does not evidence the 73-check gate
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs test:i18n, test:commerce, test:seo, test:backup, test:brand, test:brand:unit and test:e2e only; neither test:economics nor test:financial nor test:financial:unit is wired. gh pr checks 20 reports the single 'Build, test and verify' check as pass, and mergeStateStatus is UNSTABLE. S-10 only checks that package.json exposes the scripts.
findings.description: The green CI signal on PR #20 does not include the milestone gate; MC-13 acceptance depends on the manually run commands documented in this review. This is a process risk rather than a data defect.
findings.requiredCorrection: Add npm run test:financial and npm run test:financial:unit (and the inherited economics gates) to the CI workflow, or explicitly record in the delivery record that the MC-13 gate is run manually and that the CI check does not cover it.
findings.auditorReverification: Inspect the workflow and the delivery record statement.

findings.title: Disclosed model simplifications: input VAT recovered only on inventory receipts; refunds are hardware-only; opening cash is an analysis convention
findings.evidence: Engine inputVat = inventoryReceiptsCost x 21% x 100%; VAT on opex, software and capex is neither recovered nor paid. refundsAllowance is hardware-only while the MC-12 subscription direct cost already contains a returns line (disclosed in MC13-RECURRING-REVENUE-AND-SAAS-ECONOMICS.md §4 and §11). Opening cash is 0 by ASM-MC13-044 while the real company position is UNKNOWN.
findings.description: These are declared modelling choices that make the conditional financing requirement conservative in some directions and incomplete in others; they are not concealed. They must remain explicit residual risks and may not be presented as complete economics.
findings.requiredCorrection: None required for this verdict if the disclosures are retained; keep the statements in the delivery record and the executive report.
findings.auditorReverification: Confirm the disclosures survive the correction commits.

findings.title: Adversarial unit suite is coupled to the live review state and cannot pass 29/29 at the final record; the positive control already fails at the frozen commit
findings.evidence: scripts/check-marea-financial-model.test.mjs test 27 asserts 'control: the audit starts pending' - assert.equal(review.verdict, 'PENDING_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW') - and then mutates the live data.reviewFindings record. Runner results: at the frozen commit 28/29 pass and the positive control fails with D-02, D-07; after this review record was written 27/29 pass, with test 27 failing its own control assertion and the positive control still failing with V-19, D-02, D-07. MC13-EXECUTIVE-REPORT.md §I claims 'Suite adversaria: npm run test:financial:unit - 29 pruebas ... cada mutacion falla exactamente en el control previsto', but the suite as committed is red and the claimed 29/29 is unreachable even after the delivery record is added, because test 27 will always fail once a genuine review verdict is recorded.
findings.description: The negative-control suite cannot certify the final state: one test depends on the repository review record being PENDING rather than constructing its own fixture, and the positive control cannot pass while the mandatory delivery record is missing. The milestone requirement of 29/29 is therefore not met and cannot be met without a test change, regardless of the financial model.
findings.requiredCorrection: Refactor test 27 to inject a synthetic pending-review fixture (working on a clone with reviewFindings overridden) so the negative control is independent of the repository review state; keep the positive control asserting a genuine 73/73 at the final record (requires F-01 and the final verdict/manifest reconciliation); after the corrections re-run `node --test scripts/check-marea-financial-model.test.mjs` and record 29/29 with the exact output in the delivery record.
findings.auditorReverification: Run the suite at the final record state and confirm 29/29 with the positive control and test 27 independent of live data; inspect the diff for the fixture change.

residualRisks: External commercial evidence is BLOCKED_OR_NOT_OBTAINED by design: 0 formal supplier quotations, 0 executed contracts, 0 granted licensing rights, 0 customer evidence, CUSTOMER_WTP_VALIDATED = false. Every revenue, contribution, cash and break-even figure is a conditional output of labelled scenario assumptions, not a forecast.

Named unknown costs are excluded from the conditional result: data licence, product-liability insurance, CRA/security lifecycle, FLEET onboarding/DPA/SLA, CAC, validated churn/renewal, willingness to pay and the company cash/funding position. The true financing requirement is higher than every figure reported.

Opening cash is zero by analysis convention (ASM-MC13-044); the real EMBARCARTE cash position is UNKNOWN, so cumulative cash and financing requirement cannot be interpreted as the actual funding need until the opening position is known.

VAT treatment is an illustration (21% Spain, 100% recoverable input VAT on inventory receipts only, one-month lag); M60 VAT balances are paid in M61, outside the horizon, and no tax adviser has confirmed the treatment.
Demand, churn, renewal, activation, channel mix and operating-cost envelopes are ILLUSTRATIVE SCENARIO_ASSUMPTIONS; there is no validated demand and no probability is assigned to any scenario.

The 60-month horizon truncates collections: with a 2-period distributor lag the last two months of distributor invoices are not collected within the horizon, so M60 cumulative cash contains a timing artifact (28,050.84 EUR in BASE even before the F-04 correction).
FX exposure is inherited as an engineering assumption (MC-11 basis) and no hedge exists; the FX gap is disclosed, not closed (decision D-053).

Break-even thresholds are CONDITIONAL_HYPOTHETICAL_THRESHOLD or NOT_DETERMINABLE; 0 are VERIFIED. No document may promote them to a verified break-even, profitability, investment-return or launch statement.
The refund-cash and distributor-basis corrections (F-03, F-04) will change the reported cash, financing requirement and receivables; any document not regenerated afterwards becomes inconsistent.

The gate cannot currently detect a document-level false review PASS (F-02) or a missing refund-cash column (F-03); the auditor exercised both as negative controls, so process discipline plus the required validator changes are needed.

The adversarial unit suite is not independent of the repository review state (F-16): the positive control fails at the frozen commit and test 27 fails once a genuine verdict is recorded, so the claimed 29/29 cannot be reproduced and the suite cannot currently certify a final record.
whatWouldChangeVerdict: F-01: author MC-13-DELIVERY.md, update MASTER-PROMPT-REGISTRY.md row 13 and correct the decision-log evidence references in a record commit; then D-02 and the unit-suite positive control pass.

F-02: make the MC13-EXECUTIVE-REPORT.md status block equal the manifest/review verdict (PENDING_INTERNAL or the actual verdict), remove the unearned PASS, and add a validator guard against document-level false PASS claims.
F-03: settle refunds in cash (or otherwise make the treatment internally consistent), regenerate all derived files and documents, and confirm ST-07 is adverse versus the corrected base.
F-04: compute distributor invoiced/collected cash from the channel-adjusted gross price, regenerate the derived files and documents, and confirm the receivables and financing-requirement figures.

F-05..F-12 and F-13..F-16 are documentation/traceability/process/testing matters: they do not by themselves block PASS_INTERNAL_FINANCIAL_SCOPE, but the contract/validator inconsistencies in F-05, the figure corrections in F-08/F-09 and the state-dependent test suite (F-16) must be fixed in the same record commit so the gate and its unit suite can reach 73/73 and 29/29.

After corrections are committed and re-frozen (new head SHA), the auditor re-runs the independent recomputation, the 14-mutation harness, the 208-claim reconciliation and the gate; PASS_INTERNAL_FINANCIAL_SCOPE is awarded only if no BLOCKING/MAJOR finding remains open and the gate is 73/73 with the manifest/status block reconciled to the actual review verdict.

External commercial evidence is not required to change this verdict: PASS_INTERNAL_FINANCIAL_SCOPE covers the internal analytical scope only, and MC13_EXTERNAL_COMMERCIAL_VALIDATION must stay BLOCKED_OR_NOT_OBTAINED.
